acceptance: 1) In a blank browser context click footer analytics-preferences and assert the preferences panel is visible. In both the unselected and Reject-clicked states, cookies/browser storage contain no analytics identity, the POST /api/analytics/events count is 0, and product navigation/model controls still respond to clicks. Clicking Allow sends analytics=true to POST /api/analytics/consent and receives a valid signed cookie. Subsequent navigation produces page_view with this eventId in response acceptedIds; retrying the same navigationId leaves exactly one database row (E-42). 2) Disconnect the network before event transmission to create a pending queue, then click Withdraw: local analytics identity and pending-item count both become 0, and reconnecting sends none of that queue. Further navigation sends no events; the cookie is cleared, and an old pending-event request without a valid cookie after clearing returns 403. Separately delay the actual true-request response, then click false; assert serialized writes with false last, and after all responses the cookie is absent, the queue is 0 and collection does not resume. Do not backfill withdrawn-period visits (E-43). 3) At 1920x1080, 1440x900 and 390x844 retain request/interaction GIFs. Computed border width equals 2px, border radius equals 0px and accent color equals the section 11 token. Tab focuses each named control, Enter/Space operates it and each measured touch target is at least 44 CSS px. 4) Click footer privacy-link to /[locale]/privacy. The en definition contains anonymous browsers that consented to analytics, and the ru definition contains анонимных браузеров, разрешивших аналитику. Copy makes no unique-real-person/cross-device-identification claim. Isolated tests separately change device contexts, clear identifiers and switch browsers; query the backend to verify a new browserHash can form while reporting only whether it differs, not its raw value (E-45). 5) Necessary-chat, analytics-consent and cleanup-state sections are each visible on the privacy page. Retention displays configuration values: chat cookie seven days idle/30 days absolute, consultation 90 days, raw analytics 30 days/aggregates 13 months; the site-IANA text equals SiteSetting. Default cleanup state explicitly shows disabled/dry-run and that actual cleanup requires separate authorization, without treating documents/dispatch as authorization. robots/noindex still follows the existing completeness switch.

E-42.scene: C-05 Analytics collection, deduplication and retention
E-42.trigger: The user has not allowed analytics or has rejected it
E-42.expect: Do not create/store analytics identifiers or send analytics events; the site and 3D functions remain usable. The dashboard must clearly cover only consented browsers and must not turn missing nonconsented samples into a whole-site visitor count.

E-43.scene: C-05 Analytics collection, deduplication and retention
E-43.expect: Stop collection, discard unsent analytics events and clear local analytics identifiers. Do not send visits from the withdrawn-consent period afterward.

E-45.scene: C-05 Analytics collection, deduplication and retention
E-45.trigger: The same person switches devices, clears identifiers or uses another browser
E-45.expect: State Number of anonymous browsers that consented to analytics in the visitor definition/help. Separately test device switching, identifier clearing and browser switching, each of which can create a new browserHash. Do not claim unique real-person or cross-device identification.
